Theory of Knowledge 13 Jan 2022

Is there a solid justification for regarding knowledge in the natural sciences more highly than knowledge in the human sciences?

Natural sciences are the knowledge produced by scientists that aren’t fixed and can always be altered. It is the study of nature from around us on earth to the universe and beyond. Natural science is justified with predictions and theories. Human science is the study of human behaviour which is known to be complex as it is looked at through different perspectives and is harder to prove than natural science. For the other AOK, I chose to write about human science as it is an area of knowledge that competes with natural science as they are almost equally relevant in terms of justification. As they are both equally controversial where the conditions for a belief are always expanded and differences between people. 

Diverse individuals will perceive knowledge of natural sciences in several ways. They are going to have distinct arguments for valuing knowledge in the natural sciences more or less than knowledge in other AOKs. These areas of knowledge are always debatable and highly controversial, and many unique opinions flow through many different minds. All these different mindsets would eventually help us to deliver a balanced argument that has many considerations with many points of view and includes analytical explanations of certain knowledge. That is the reason for the untrust of both sciences’ justification. 

Is there a solid justification regarding knowledge in the natural sciences more highly than knowledge in human science? Natural sciences rely exclusively on empirical knowledge or pure logic. “It is not simply a collection of facts; rather it is a path to understanding.” (Berkeley.edu, 2021). Scientists work in various approaches, but all science relies on testing theories by figuring out what expectations are produced by a theory and making observations to determine whether those expectations could be true or make sense. The same thing relates to human science but in human sciences, ethics is involved more than natural science. Experimenting for human sciences is mostly unethical, and risky. Is knowledge more highly regarded in natural sciences? Is solid justification and proof the same? Does a singular natural science make more use of the scientific method than others?

The Earth expansion theory is a hypothesis that declares that continents' position and relative movement is partially due to the volume of the Earth increasing. This theory was hypothesised back in the 19th century. Back then, they didn’t have the necessary level of scientific knowledge and at the time the amount of data available in many scientific fields was very limited. The lack of sufficient technologies is also linked with the level of justification. Geologists and physicists generally acknowledged that planets’ dimensions could be altered, even though the change of volume was believed to happen because of a contraction, not an expansion. Laszlo Egyed, a professor at the Geophysical Institute, based on variations of the sea level in the geological past, proposed that the earth was slowly and constantly growing, back in 1956. According to him, today’s continents are the remains of an ancient crust of a smaller planet, surrounded by fresher rocks generated along with cracks at the mid-ocean ridges. He explained that the increase in the volume of our planet occurs by modifications of mineral phases in the earth's inner core, as minerals are known to change the structure of crystals via the change in heat and pressure. In 1966, another explanation was suggested by German physicist Pascual Jordan. He hypothesised that the expansion of the earth was imputable to the general dilatation of the space-time continuum. However, the Expanding Earth hypothesis fails to provide a persuasive mechanism to explain the increase of the earth's mass or volume over time. Also, simple measurements of the circumference of the earth using satellites, could disprove, or prove an increase in the radius of the earth. In 1912, Alfred Wegener proposed to use modern satellite measurements that are accurate enough to show the movements of the earth's plates, however, failed to find any real evidence for expanding earth, except on the internet. How solid is using the internet on theories? The short answer is that it is very unstable as the internet would just create more contradictions due to it not supporting proper scientific testing.

Another theory, the Big Bang theory, “The origin of the cosmos” was thought of by Georges Lemaitre, a Belgian cosmologist and Catholic priest. The Big Bang theory is an explanation for how the universe started. It states that the universe started with an infinitely hot and dense single point that inflated and stretched at unimaginable velocities. Our technology can’t examine the universe's birth, much of what we understand about the Big Bang comes from mathematical formulas. Paul Sutter is an astrophysicist and states that there are five pieces of evidence that the Big Bang was true. Firstly, the night sky is dark, this is where he explains that because our universe is infinite anything could happen. He states that it is inevitable that the Big Bang happened due to how random and infinite the universe is. Secondly, he states that our universe was different in the past than it is now, thus, we don’t understand its randomness back then. Thirdly he explains how the universe is constantly expanding which increases the chances of the Big Bang occurring. Fourthly, he declares that as the universe expands, it will cool to a point where electrons can settle around nuclei, making the first complete atoms of hydrogen and helium. Which is how the universe started. Lastly, “the universe expanded and cooled from the frenetic first few minutes of its existence” (Sutter, 2018). This whole research is all based on theories as it isn’t possible to experiment on what he had stated, this doesn’t show any solid justification. This also indicates how highly natural science is viewed but yet still illustrates the controversy between the sciences. This is a case where he is using theories on a single theory. How solid and reliable can this hypothesis be?

Great minds have disproved this theory, we spend all this time trying to gain knowledge of what the point of life is. This perfectly explains how we focus more on natural science than human science. But even if that is the case both AOKs don’t seem to have any reliable justification. Stephen Hawking is one of the world’s greatest minds. Disproved the Big Bang theory and theorised that the Universe Had No Beginning, he stated a proposal on how the universe might have arisen from nothing. ” Asking what came before the Big Bang … would be like asking what lies south of the South Pole.”- Stephen Hawking (Quanta Magazine, 2019). This shows how non-reliable natural science can be, no matter who the individual is, they will probably have a different opinion on things. Is there a solid justification regarding knowledge in the human sciences more highly than knowledge in natural science?

Knowledge in the human sciences is more challenging to experiment on as there is no way to look inside or see in an individual's thoughts and intellectual processes that affect their behaviour, mindset, and choices. Human behaviour is difficult to study and test experiments, human behaviour is almost random as everyone’s mind works and thinks differently. This by itself proves how human science doesn’t have any solid justification and is a reason why it could potentially be viewed less than natural science. Another proof is:

Are murderers born or made? What drives people to kill?

Dr Cesare Lombroso in the 1870s stated that criminals aren’t on the same level as ‘normal’ beings in the evolutionary ladder. But they are a “reversion to a primitive or subhuman type of man” (News, 2015). He concluded that you could tell a criminal by the shape of their face and the length of their arms. Unfortunately, as expected, spotting potential murderers isn’t as simple as Dr Lombroso hypothesised and then his "scientific" findings were condemned. But this was the beginning of discovering if criminals/murderers have different brains from the rest. Even though here human science wasn’t solid, it has still started a discussable topic, that might develop more theories. The invention of brain scanning back in the 80s revolutionised our understanding of what goes on inside our minds. The first scanning study of criminals/murderers was carried out by British neuroscientist Prof Adrian Raine. Many years of scanning the brains of various criminals/murderers and virtually all showed similar brain changes. There was reduced activity in the brain which controls emotional impulses, and the area which produces our emotions. So, it seems that murderers have brains that make them more inclined to rage and anger, while also making them less able to control themselves. The first theory that got condemned started and discovered this knowledge via technology. Therefore, even if a theory shows to be unsolid, it still becomes a starting point for knowledge.

To conclude, even though Natural science is as theoretical as human science, it is viewed more highly than human science as Natural science could help us find out the reason for our existence, while human science focuses on human behaviour. Both sciences are still hard to view as it is sometimes inhumane or impossible to experiment. Human sciences and Natural sciences are mostly conducted by theories and predictions, they are inaccurate and rarely considered a fact. Even though I have stated that Natural science is viewed more highly, I think that both AOKs don’t have a significant difference in terms of solid justifications, as both don’t have any solid validations due to their having difficulty finding sufficient reason to prove the knowledge or an instance to be reasonable.
